title: One of my friends is
goal: Match the verb with the real subject
wm: Agreement of the Verb with the Subject
intro: The verb must agree with its subject: singular subject, singular verb. Trouble starts when other words come between them (“The list of items are…”) or with words like each, everyone, one of, and the number of. Find the real subject, then choose the verb.

rules.rule: Find the main noun. Words after “of” don’t change it.
examples: The price of vegetables is high.
One of my friends lives in Dubai.

rules.rule: each, every, everyone, somebody, nobody → singular.
“The number of” → singular. “A number of” (= many) → plural.
examples: The number of cars is growing.
A number of people were waiting.

rules.rule: Two subjects joined by “and” → plural. With “or / nor”, match the nearer one.
examples: My brother and sister live abroad.
Neither the manager nor the staff were told.

mistakes.wrong: One of my friends are coming.
mistakes.right: One of my friends is coming.

mistakes.wrong: The quality of these products are good.
mistakes.right: The quality of these products is good.

mistakes.wrong: The number of students have increased.
mistakes.right: The number of students has increased.

ex.q: One of the lights ___ not working.
The list of names ___ on the wall.
A number of problems ___ come up.
Rice and dal ___ my favourite meal.
ex.y: One dish thought of as one thing: is.

ex.q: Each of the rooms have a balcony.
ex.fixed: Each of the rooms has a balcony.

ex.q: The cost of these phones are too high.
ex.fixed: The cost of these phones is too high.

ex.a: One of my colleagues is from Assam.

ex.q: Correct this: “One of my cousin are a pilot.”
a: One of my cousins is a pilot

talk: Talk about your team or class: how many people there are, what everyone does, and describe one of your friends there.
